title: Spring Boot Basics and REST Controllers
description: What Spring Boot adds to Spring, generating and reading a Boot project, dependency injection and bean scopes, how auto-configuration works, and REST controllers with path, query and body parameters, ResponseEntity status codes and an OpenAPI description explored in Swagger UI.
sourceCoverageNotes: Course slice: Standard S1-S13 and Fast FT1-FT8. This module covers Standard S1-S2.
Module grouping is a second-mate grouping decision (closing source-gap-spring-boot-modules), not syllabus: modules follow calendar day sequence, S1-S2 here.
Fast mapping: FT1 rows 0-5 and FT2 rows 1-3 map to these topics; '(skim)' suffixes are Fast emphasis metadata, not separate pages.

Module coding lab (captain-approved addition beyond the S1-S2 Concept-day overlay): required Standard real-toolchain practice at coding-lab/ with at least one tested task for each of the nine taught topics (trackRequirement standard required, fast not-required), mvn -q -o test, Spring Boot 4.1.2, no database, no container engine; Fast skips coding labs.

Standard placement: the required module coding lab runs on S2 in the frozen Concept-day 40-minute 'Faded, then fresh problem' coding-lab block (curriculum/snapshot/pep-calendar.json dayTypes.Concept), after the four S2 pages, so it follows reading-an-openapi-spec-and-exploring-it-in-swagger-ui, the module's final taught topic (S2, fourth of four), and closes the module before porting-and-configuration starts on S3. Authoring estimate, not piloted, with 1 minute of slack: no S2 topic links a video, so the four pages (58 minutes) fill Reading, Short video, Worked example and Short exercises (55) and 3 minutes of that block, and the lab's 36 task minutes fill 36 of the remaining 37, so S2 stays within 120 minutes; the one-time online setup (mvn -q dependency:go-offline, about 8 minutes) is done before the block, as in html-css-js/dom-tooling-and-async. The lab sits outside the calendar's lab overlay, because S2 is a Concept day with requiredLab false, but inside a Concept-day block whose calendar format is coding lab. This supersedes the intake's no-lab statement for spring-boot-basics (authoring/evidence/spring-boot/intake.md, section Lab plan), which is left for a course-level follow-up branch.

Partial objective coverage in the module coding lab (recorded): every taught topic has at least one tested task, and some objectives are only partly exercised. For dependency-injection-replacing-manual-wiring#o1 it replaces one manual new in the controller with constructor injection of a configured bean; wiring across controller, service and repository layers is taught by constructor-injection-across-layers and applied in the porting-and-configuration module lab on S3-S4. For response-codes-with-responseentity#o1 it practices 200, 201 with Location and 404 but not 204, which the page's editor activity (a DELETE handler returning noContent) covers. For spring-vs-spring-boot-what-boot-adds#o2, Task 9 tests the embedded server started from main; the BOM-managed parent and starter appear in the shipped pom without a dedicated check. For generating-a-spring-boot-project-and-its-structure#o2, Task 6 tests only where application.properties lives. For how-auto-configuration-works#o1, Task 7 tests component scanning through scanBasePackages; the condition objectives stay on the page. For reading-an-openapi-spec-and-exploring-it-in-swagger-ui#o1, Task 8 implements one GET operation from a shipped OpenAPI document, with no request body; springdoc and Swagger UI (o2, o3) stay on the page, because the lab pom and its offline setup are unchanged. Task 8 also adds the required query parameter and its 400 that path-query-and-body-parameters#o1 and #o2 name.

Practice mastery check authored at assessments/spring-boot-basics-mastery-check/ (blueprint plus learner-visible practice.gift, ungraded, 15 minutes at most); the graded course final is the separate course-level blueprint spring-boot/assessments/spring-boot-final-assessment.
